subject.title: fix(cron): default deleteAfterRun for isolated cron jobs

question: Should recurring isolated cron jobs be cleanup-safe by default, or should `deleteAfterRun` remain a one-shot-only cron lifecycle contract?
rationale: This PR and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/96045 encode opposite product contracts, and the choice affects existing cron state, future defaults, and session-retention behavior.

options.title: Complete recurring isolated cleanup
options.body: Keep this PR's direction, but add a persisted-row or doctor path for existing omitted jobs and reconcile the strict-validation PR before merge.

options.title: Choose one-shot-only delete-after-run
options.body: Pause or close this PR and continue through the strict-validation direction after its caller and upgrade blockers are resolved.

options.title: Accept fresh-create-only behavior
options.body: Land only the new default while explicitly documenting that already-persisted omitted jobs require operator action or a later migration.

recommendation.title: Complete recurring isolated cleanup
recommendation.body: Keep this PR's direction, but add a persisted-row or doctor path for existing omitted jobs and reconcile the strict-validation PR before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision crosses cron store compatibility, default semantics, and upgrade behavior where this history points to recent ownership.
